studies.label: Pairit ad-creation experiment (human-AI versus human-human teams), with human and AI evaluations and a subsequent ad campaign on X
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Individuals were randomized before matching (PDF p. 14, Section 3.3); teams were formed afterward. Participant regressions report heteroskedasticity-robust SEs without team clustering. Human and AI quality regressions cluster SEs by ad, not creator or team (PDF pp. 22, 47, 49, 51-52). Team productivity uses one observation per team and robust SEs (PDF p. 47, Table B).

arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: A participant collaborates with an autonomous GPT-4o agent in a shared workspace. The agent chats, edits copy, selects images, and generates images through Dall-E 3; the human submits the ads. Partner identity is disclosed after the task (PDF pp. 11-12, 14-15).

arms.name: Human-Human
arms.description: A participant collaborates with another participant in the same shared workspace. Both have access to Dall-E 3 image generation; submitted ads require both participants to confirm. This is an active human-partner comparison (PDF pp. 11, 14-15).

studies.task: Create display advertisements for a think tank report by writing a headline, primary text, and description and selecting or generating an image during a timed collaborative session (PDF pp. 11, 14-16).

ai_tool.name: OpenAI gpt-4o-2024-08-06 agent; Dall-E 3 API for image generation, available in both arms
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 3.2 (Context), dated GPT-4o model identifier; PDF p. 11, Section 3.1, shared Dall-E 3 access

preregistration.where: osf.io/jfzha and osf.io/95dhu (PDF p. 11, footnote 1); field campaigns also described as preregistered at osf.io/95dhu (PDF p. 18, Section 3.9).

open_items: The PDF does not supply unambiguous total or arm-specific counts at randomization, the assignment ratio, or attrition by arm. Its abstract describes the analyzed cohort as randomized; the detailed flow distinguishes entrants, completers, and exclusions without consistent allocation counts (PDF pp. 1, 14-16). n_randomized is null.

Participant-flow and human-human team totals conflict in the source. Completers, excluded sessions, final analyzed people, reported attrition, and Table 1 team counts do not reconcile. Retain the printed analyzed people rather than repair counts arithmetically (PDF pp. 15-16).

The text-submitting diversity sample has a printed total but no arm-specific people counts. It also has no observed arm means, participant SDs, or arm-specific uncertainty; the regression intercept is conditional on covariates and is not an observed mean (PDF pp. 21-22).

No eligible outcome has a printed participant-level SD or usable standardized effect. All arm means are unreported as descriptive means; regression intercepts have not been relabeled or combined with coefficients to obtain levels. No standardized effect or interval was calculated.

The exact number of creative-task participants contributing to the human-rating and AI-rating regressions is not printed. Rating/output observation counts must not be treated as participant counts, and people who produced no output cannot automatically be included (PDF pp. 17, 22, and 52).
Rater recruitment, survey entry, and completed-rating totals are not reconciled by the paper. No retained-rater count is derived from them (PDF p. 17, Section 3.8; PDF p. 22, Table 2).

The paper does not explain attribution of jointly confirmed ads to human-human partners. Participant models report robust rather than team-clustered SEs, and rating models cluster by ad rather than participant/team. Team productivity uses a different aggregation and has inconsistent people/team counts; appropriate precision for synthesis remains unresolved (PDF pp. 15-16, 19, 22, 47, 49, and 51-52).
Ad-copy completion has no stated numerator, denominator, or scoring/coding procedure. Its measure code is null pending that information (PDF pp. 48-49, Appendix E).

The preregistrations are named, but the PDF does not identify their preregistered primary outcome. The paper calls productivity, quality, and diversity primary in its results section; that does not establish preregistered-primary status (PDF pp. 11, 18, and 21).

The excluded field analyses have inconsistent corpus/sample counts and do not define the actual rows behind the view-metric observation count. No field row unit or creative-participant count can be inferred (PDF pp. 16, 18-20, 25, and 53).
The paper provides analysis data and code only upon request; the GitHub link is rating-survey software, not posted analysis data. No data-derived statistics were used (PDF pp. 17 and 39).
notes: Extraction A, 2026-10-10. Read all 116133 characters of the markdown in consecutive chunks, including references and Appendices A-L. Checked PDF text with pymupdf for every cited results and methods page and recovered the table structure with text-based find_tables where useful. PDF and printed page numbers coincide. The field campaign evaluates outputs of the same creative-task cohort and is not a second AI-assignment study. The comparison is ai_vs_active: a GPT-4o teammate versus another person, with Dall-E 3 access shared across arms; there is no human-alone arm. All estimates describe outputs created while assistance was available. Later ratings or ad campaigns are not after_ai transfer tests. Separate records retain distinct full-sample adjusted/unadjusted or participant/team specifications. Exact repeats between Table 2 and Tables B/G are recorded once. Both quality-only field models and treatment models with post-treatment controls are excluded. In particular, Table I columns 1 and 4 still adjust for later campaign spend even though they omit quality ratings; the screening form is a map, and extraction rule 5 controls this decision. Unreported p-values are null; significance bounds are transcribed from the table legends without calculation. Source quotes retain the printed precision and signs. Null arm means are deliberate: neither adjusted intercepts nor unadjusted intercepts labeled only as such were reclassified as observed means. No source-verified shared sample is identified in the screening form.
